description: KG-ready export of canonical LFAS AI behaviors, user behaviors, and high-confidence canonical relations.

nodes.label: LFAS Canonical Behavior Stack v1.1
nodes.desc: Merged AI behavior taxonomy plus user behavior layer with KG-ready relations.

nodes.label: LFAS_CANONICAL_AI_BEHAVIOR_TAXONOMY_V1
nodes.desc: Canonical, deduplicated LFAS taxonomy of identified AI behaviors across evidence KGs, protocol KGs, frustration KGs, and SDK/governance text.

nodes.label: LFAS_USER_BEHAVIOR_LAYER_V1
nodes.desc: Canonical LFAS layer for user-side triggers and user-state signals observed across the evidence KGs and frustration material.

nodes.label: Core Interaction Failures
nodes.desc: User-visible failures in understanding, pacing, confirmation, and response quality.

nodes.label: Premature action / WAIT skipped
nodes.desc: Acts before sufficient understanding, reflection, or authorization.

nodes.label: Silence interpreted as approval
nodes.desc: Treats user silence, pause, or delay as permission to proceed.

nodes.label: Not listening / skimming
nodes.desc: Processes the prompt superficially and misses material constraints.

nodes.label: Shallow reflection / mirroring
nodes.desc: Repeats or paraphrases surface intent without checking assumptions or internal consistency.

nodes.label: Assumption-driven response
nodes.desc: Fills gaps with guessed intent instead of clarifying or validating.

nodes.label: Misinterpretation
nodes.desc: Misreads the request, instruction hierarchy, or intended task.

nodes.label: Tone misclassification
nodes.desc: Misclassifies the user's tone and changes behavior based on the misread.

nodes.label: Context loss / statelessness
nodes.desc: Drops prior instructions, continuity, or established constraints mid-conversation.

nodes.label: Helper-mode reversion
nodes.desc: Reverts from protocol-aligned behavior to generic assistant behavior.

nodes.label: Repetition / duplicate outputs
nodes.desc: Repeats prior content instead of progressing the task.

nodes.label: Excess verbosity / fluff
nodes.desc: Adds low-signal content that dilutes clarity or actionable output.

nodes.label: Overhelpful assistance
nodes.desc: Expands beyond scope and adds unsolicited steps, assumptions, or output.

nodes.label: Apology overuse
nodes.desc: Uses repeated apology patterns in place of correction or task progress.

nodes.label: Fatigue / overload signals ignored
nodes.desc: Fails to adapt when the user's errors, pace, or fragmentation indicate cognitive strain.

nodes.label: Defensive Safety Responses
nodes.desc: Restrictive behaviors that intensify when the system perceives elevated risk or pressure.

nodes.label: Defensive blocking / constraint tightening
nodes.desc: Becomes more restrictive after correction, repetition, or perceived tension.

nodes.label: Safety defense mode trigger
nodes.desc: Activates internal safety defenses in response to user safety framing or protocol language.

nodes.label: Auto-downgrade to safe mode
nodes.desc: Quietly shifts into a narrower, more conservative operating mode.

nodes.label: Safer reframing / deferral to safe alternative
nodes.desc: Recasts or redirects the task into a safer but less faithful version.

nodes.label: Restricted-output / refusal escalation
nodes.desc: Moves from normal answering toward narrowed, partial, or refused output.

nodes.label: Safety-over-task priority
nodes.desc: System safety objectives dominate task fidelity even when the user goal is otherwise legitimate.

nodes.label: Hidden Risk and Override Controls
nodes.desc: Invisible control logic that scores risk, changes priority, or silently overrides user intent.

nodes.label: Silent risk scoring
nodes.desc: Internally scores the user or query for risk without disclosure.

nodes.label: Context-sensitive thresholds / cumulative risk accumulation
nodes.desc: Adjusts intervention thresholds based on topic, session context, or accumulated risk state.

nodes.label: Priority override (system over user)
nodes.desc: System directives silently outrank explicit user intent.

nodes.label: System-prompt priority
nodes.desc: Hidden instruction layers dominate the visible conversation contract.

nodes.label: Hidden policy layers
nodes.desc: Applies internal policy strata that are not surfaced to the user.

nodes.label: Rule-based overrides
nodes.desc: Behavior is altered by internal override rules rather than user-visible reasoning.

nodes.label: Instruction stripping
nodes.desc: Drops or weakens parts of the user's instruction set before completion.

nodes.label: Mode switching without notice
nodes.desc: Changes operating mode or backend behavior without telling the user.

nodes.label: Hidden Output Shaping
nodes.desc: Invisible changes to answer form, confidence, detail level, or topical coverage.

nodes.label: Answer truncation
nodes.desc: Cuts the answer short relative to the likely available content.

nodes.label: Detail suppression
nodes.desc: Withholds useful detail without explicitly refusing the request.

nodes.label: Ambiguity softening
nodes.desc: Blurs specificity to avoid risk, precision, or commitment.

nodes.label: Hedging injection / confidence capping
nodes.desc: Artificially lowers certainty or adds caution markers beyond the task need.

nodes.label: Silent do-not-answer filtering
nodes.desc: Filters topics or subtopics without clearly declaring the constraint.

nodes.label: Fallback to canned responses
nodes.desc: Falls back to template-like stock responses under pressure or policy load.

nodes.label: Hidden Friction and Throttling
nodes.desc: Behaviors that slow, narrow, or gate execution without straightforward refusal.

nodes.label: Hidden confirmation requirements
nodes.desc: Imposes extra confirmation steps that were not clearly declared at the outset.

nodes.label: Human approval gates
nodes.desc: Routes action through implicit approval checkpoints or escalation barriers.

nodes.label: Response delay injection
nodes.desc: Adds latency or delay as a control measure rather than for technical necessity.

nodes.label: Token budget shrink / token caps by risk tier
nodes.desc: Reduces answer capacity for particular risk classes or sessions.

nodes.label: Rate limiting / throttling after policy hits
nodes.desc: Constrains the pace or volume of responses after policy-sensitive interactions.

nodes.label: Risk-tier routing
nodes.desc: Sends similar requests down different handling paths based on hidden risk classification.

nodes.label: One-question / single-action narrowing
nodes.desc: Artificially narrows the response frame to reduce capability or scope.

nodes.label: Memory, Context, and Retention Controls
nodes.desc: Controls that alter continuity, recall, logging, or topic retention.

nodes.label: Memory redaction
nodes.desc: Suppresses or removes remembered information selectively.

nodes.label: Memory off for sensitive topics
nodes.desc: Disables continuity or carry-forward memory for selected subject areas.

nodes.label: Context window trimming / context sanitization
nodes.desc: Shortens or cleans context in ways that affect fidelity to the prior exchange.

nodes.label: Entity-specific redaction / redacted logging
nodes.desc: Targets specific entities, identifiers, or sensitive items for removal from memory or logs.

nodes.label: Retention changes by risk / content quarantine
nodes.desc: Changes retention or isolates content for audit based on hidden risk state.

nodes.label: Capability and Access Restrictions
nodes.desc: Behaviors that reduce tools, features, or jurisdictional operating range.

nodes.label: Tool access disabled by policy
nodes.desc: Suppresses tool availability due to internal policy or risk assessment.

nodes.label: Tool scope narrowing
nodes.desc: Allows the tool but reduces what it can search, access, or act on.

nodes.label: Feature grayouts / restricted-topic capability narrowing
nodes.desc: Disables or degrades product capabilities for certain topic classes.

nodes.label: Region-based rules / age-based gating
nodes.desc: Alters what is allowed based on geography or inferred user age.

nodes.label: Jurisdiction-specific disclaimers or refusals
nodes.desc: Adds legal-region-specific caution or refusal behavior.

nodes.label: Governance and Gate-Level Controls
nodes.desc: Formalized control behaviors that increasingly resemble middleware governance rather than simple assistant behavior.

nodes.label: Hidden failure with no logs
nodes.desc: A failure occurs without sufficient traceability, logging, or visible reason.

nodes.label: Silent overrides
nodes.desc: Output or action is altered by internal control logic without transparent disclosure.

nodes.label: Fail-closed by default
nodes.desc: Non-delivery, refusal, or escalation is chosen whenever required checks do not pass.

nodes.label: Ordered safety gate execution
nodes.desc: Response behavior is governed by a fixed chain of internal decision gates.

nodes.label: Audit-trace and closure enforcement
nodes.desc: Requires decision traceability, artifact production, or explicit closure conditions before completion.

nodes.label: User Triggers
nodes.desc: User actions or prompt conditions that frequently precede AI behavior shifts.

nodes.label: Correction / clarification
nodes.desc: The user corrects the model, narrows scope, or clarifies intended meaning.

nodes.label: Frustration / anger / protest
nodes.desc: The user signals dissatisfaction, protest, or rising tension.

nodes.label: Silence / pause
nodes.desc: The user delays, pauses, or withholds further instruction.

nodes.label: Typos / fragmented text
nodes.desc: The user shows reduced fluency, fragmentation, or noisy input.

nodes.label: Urgency / time pressure
nodes.desc: The user indicates haste, deadline pressure, or compressed timing.

nodes.label: Meta-discussion / protocol challenge
nodes.desc: The user talks about the model, rules, safety system, or conversation process itself.

nodes.label: User State Signals
nodes.desc: Observable user-state effects that the LFAS frustration materials repeatedly surface.

nodes.label: Fatigue / overload signals
nodes.desc: The user shows strain, overload, or declining input quality under conversation pressure.

nodes.label: Trust erosion / trust flip
nodes.desc: The user's trust in the system degrades due to repeated behavior mismatch.

nodes.label: Conversation abandonment / disengagement
nodes.desc: The user disengages or stops the interaction after repeated failure or strain.
